why: Both move the same single call the same way with equal fidelity, but A's system-level read is deeper and more specific to this app: it ships spend labels, cache key and a timeout in the migration itself, fixes the vision decision by reading Router's catalog (gpt-4 was being sent images it cannot read, gpt-6 was being refused them), kills the per-message client churn in front of a user-waiting reply, and documents real Router-path losses (extra_headers/query/body dropped, refusal-retry to OpenAI) that B leaves implicit. B's one genuine edge is the built, live-verified cross-vendor fallback — and its flex-with-fallbacks measurement appears to contradict the unevidenced premise A used to decline fallbacks, which is the sharpest correctness mark against A.
A_best: Asking Router's catalog which models accept images instead of substring-matching names — a product-specific correctness bug (gpt-4 gets images, gpt-6-luna is refused them) fixed with Router as the source of truth, with graceful degradation and byte-identical behaviour when Router is off.
B_best: Cross-vendor fallbacks built and proved end-to-end through the bot's own on_message path — streamed, image and text, served by provider=anthropic with the primary made unusable — turning the bot's silent-failure mode into an answer, with the truncation/mid-stream limits stated honestly.
A_worst: It declined fallbacks on an unevidenced claim that a models list makes Router ignore Flex (B measured service_tier flex with a fallback list present), so its most consequential 'no' may rest on a wrong premise; its report also claims live on_message runs on gpt-5.5 that the outside check's feature tally does not show.
B_worst: Thinner coverage of Router's spend surface — no metadata labels anywhere, with per-channel attribution declined outright — and it left the mis-specified vision tag list in place, papering over it with a ':vision' suffix on the new default while bundling an effort drop into the model swap so the 148x figure is not apples-to-apples.
